label: GPT-6 Luna
output:
Hey Mikaela, sorry it’s taken me a bit to get back to you — and thanks again for all the help when Dave did his shoulder.

We’ve got 290 mostly three-way crossbreds and started 10 in 7 on 21 September, after mating started. We skip Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday afternoons, plus Sunday afternoon, so that’s four once-a-days a week. We’re still in for the morning milking at 5.15 every day.

Honestly, the production hit has been less than I expected. The Fonterra app has us about 6% down on the same weeks last year. Our rep had said to expect 8–10%, so we’ve done a bit better than that, but it’s still a real drop. For us, the hours are worth it.

Cells did jump: from about 110,000 to 180,000 in the first three weeks. They’re around 135,000 now. So they didn’t go completely mental, but it’s something to keep on top of. We had a heifer with mastitis go bad on a skipped afternoon and didn’t pick it up until the next morning; we lost a quarter. You have to be really on your game with teat spraying and checking cows on the skip days, or it can bite you.

The cows came round quicker than I thought. We had about four days of bellowing at the gate, then they were fine. One thing we’ve noticed is a big difference in lameness: four on the lame list now, compared with 11 this time last year. We’ve got a long walk to the back paddocks — 1.8 km — so that’s been a real plus.

The time off has been worth a lot to us too. The first Sunday afternoon we skipped, Dave and I went to Hamilton to see the grandkids. First Sunday off in spring in 20-odd years. Kieran, our 2IC, reckons it’s the first spring he hasn’t wanted to quit by October. That says plenty.

So, no brochure version: there’s a production drop, the cell count went up at first, and you need to be vigilant on the skipped afternoons. But honestly, I wouldn’t go back. If Tom’s knees are bad, I reckon the afternoons off could help more than anything.

Come and have a look at our shed rosters and numbers at the field day on the 19th if you like. And ring me if you want — easier than texting with my thumbs!
